clue.text: Musical instruction for playing toccatas

indicators.note: playing about with the letters of toccatas means rearranging them

explanation.surface: A score marking tells a pianist how to play a set of toccatas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' signals an anagram of TOCCATAS; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Staccato is a direction on a score telling the performer to play notes short and detached.

clue.text: Alone with the Sun, see?

parts.note: Sol is the Latin name for the Sun
Ely is a cathedral city whose bishop's diocese is a see

explanation.surface: Someone asks a companion to look at the Sun on its own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' looks like a command but is a bishop's diocese; ELY is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Solely means only, by oneself, without others.

clue.text: Just about making St- Malo

indicators.note: making signals that the letters of the town name are reworked into a new word

explanation.surface: A ferry nearly reaches the Breton port of St Malo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' signals an anagram of ST MALO, a French port.
explanation.definitionFit: Almost means nearly, very close to.

clue.text: Willing to accept the burden

definitions.meaning: being satisfied, happy to go along with something
burden in the sense of the gist or main substance of a speech

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is satisfied and agreeable; the other is the substance or subject matter of a text, as burden means its theme.

clue.text: Person getting into knots causing a row

definitions.meaning: someone who ties knots, one who ties
a level or rank, as in seating

explanation.surface: Someone tangling themselves up starts an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: One who ties is a tier; seats in banked lines are tiers, so a row.

clue.text: Foreign article discovered in food

indicators.note: an item discovered in the food is sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a dish is a serving of food
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Something alien is found in a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign' is the definition at the front, not a description of the article; 'discovered in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Danish describes something from Denmark, which is foreign to a British solver.

clue.text: A point a top man finds exciting

parts.note: W is west, a compass point
a king is the man at the top

explanation.surface: A ruler gets thrilled by a sharp observation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exciting' is the definition, used as a verb: to awake feelings is to excite them.
explanation.definitionFit: Awaking used transitively means rousing or stirring up, as exciting means.

clue.text: A mounted soldier can overturn one on firing

indicators.note: in a down clue a mounted word is lifted up, so read from bottom to top

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: to overturn the word for can is to turn it upside down, reading it backwards in a down clue

parts.note: a tin is a can
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cavalryman might knock over a cannon as it fires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted' reverses GI to IG and 'overturn' reverses TIN to NIT. 'A' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignition is the setting alight of fuel, as in an engine's firing.

clue.text: Fine an employee taking part

indicators.note: one piece taking another adds it on behind

parts.note: a hand is a worker
some means a part or portion

explanation.surface: A worker who joins in is fined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like a penalty but is the adjective good-looking; 'an' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsome means good-looking or generous, fine in both senses.

clue.text: He'll make complaint by and about people in general

indicators.note: one piece placed about another wraps around it

parts.note: by and by is an old phrase meaning in a while, later
men can mean humankind, people in general

explanation.surface: A grumbler keeps moaning about humanity at large.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by and by' is an old-fashioned way of saying later, in due course; 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who laments voices grief or grievance, so a lamenter is a complainer.

clue.text: Caught a girl on the rebound

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Ann is a girl's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone snapped up a woman just after her break-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'on the rebound' as romantic recovery; in billiards a cannon is a ball glancing off another.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannon in billiards is a ricochet of the cue ball off one ball onto another, a kind of bounce.

clue.text: Putting intelligence first — a bloomer

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Putting intelligence first — a bloomer': GEN gives intelligence, but nothing in the words as held supplies ISTA; a word appears lost.

clue.text: The French look for somebody to rent the property

parts.note: les is French for 'the' in the plural
to see is to look

explanation.surface: A French landlord searches for a tenant.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessee is the party who holds a lease, the tenant paying to occupy a property.

clue.text: Acts as arbitrator-deems it a mistake

indicators.note: a mistake in writing the letters of deems it a jumbles them into a new order

explanation.surface: A referee calls something an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistake' signals an anagram of DEEMS IT A.
explanation.definitionFit: To mediate is to step between disputing parties as a go-between to settle the quarrel.

clue.text: Quite an unreliable old thing

indicators.note: unreliable letters will not stay put, so quite an is rearranged

explanation.surface: An old possession proves rather untrustworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unreliable' signals an anagram of QUITE AN.
explanation.definitionFit: An antique is a collector's object from a past era.

clue.text: Substitute train for strap hangers only?

parts.note: a stand-in is a substitute
to groom someone is to train or prepare them

explanation.surface: A replacement train is laid on only for commuters hanging from straps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like a railway carriage but is the verb to prepare. Strap hangers are passengers on their feet holding the overhead straps.
explanation.definitionFit: Space where passengers must stay upright, as on a crowded train or bus, is what such commuters get.

clue.text: Make a song about twit using a needle

indicators.note: one piece placed about another wraps it

parts.note: to sing is to make a song
to twit is to tease or mock

explanation.surface: Someone sings about a fool while sewing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twit' looks like a fool but is the verb to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: Smocking is decorative needlework that gathers cloth into tight pleats.

clue.text: Working for others, they'll get nice break in time

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other

parts.note: an age is a long time

indicators.note: to break the letters of nice is to shatter them into a new order

explanation.surface: Agents earn a pleasant breather in their schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' is the anagram signal on 'nice', and 'they'll get' joins wordplay to definition; 'time' gives a long period, not a clock reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Agencies are firms acting on behalf of clients.

clue.text: Attractive recording equipment!

parts.note: attractive in the sense of pulling iron, a magnet's property, together with the strip a recorder uses

explanation.definitionFit: Recorders once stored sound on plastic ribbon coated with iron oxide, read by a magnetic head.

clue.text: From the start certain military personnel will be fanatical

parts.note: ex is Latin for from

indicators.note: the start of the word the is its opening letter

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Some soldiers turn zealous right from the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' gives EX and 'the start' gives the first letter of 'the'; REME is a British army engineering corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme views are fanatical ones, far beyond the moderate.

clue.text: A church official, parking on the verge, had a meal

parts.note: P stands for parking on road signs
a rim is an edge or verge
ate means had a meal

explanation.surface: A churchman parks on the roadside grass to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'verge' reads as roadside grass but means an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A primate is an archbishop, the senior cleric of a province.

clue.text: The man who's learned a vehicle may be left in the street

indicators.note: something left in another is placed inside it

parts.note: St is short for street
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A scholar parks his van in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A savant is a scholar or sage, a person of great learning.

clue.text: People of some standing get a key to the door

parts.note: G is a musical key
an entry is a doorway

explanation.surface: Upper-class folk acquire a latchkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' reads as a latchkey but is a musical key; 'get' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentry are the class just below the nobility, people of good social position.

clue.text: One's curt when correct, showing resolve

indicators.note: to correct the letters of one's curt is to put them into a different, proper order

explanation.surface: A brusque person, once set right, shows determination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correct' signals an anagram of ONES CURT; 'when' and 'showing' are links. 'resolve' reads as determination but means work out the sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To construe is to interpret, to work out the meaning of words, which is to resolve them.

clue.text: It's sanctimonious to judge a plagiarist

parts.note: pi is informal British for piously self-righteous
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: Condemning a copycat is called holier-than-thou.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate copies others' work without permission, as a plagiarist steals writing.

clue.text: Spend unwisely, being depressed

explanation.surface: Wasting money leaves someone feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: To blue cash is old British slang for wasting it; feeling blue means feeling sad.

clue.text: Some flair is essential for arranging flowers

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A florist needs a certain flair to arrange a bouquet.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'for arranging', but that phrase is surface padding: only 'flowers' defines the answer, and 'for arranging' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: Irises are garden plants with sword-shaped leaves and showy blooms.

clue.text: A country person about 50 can be charming

indicators.note: one piece placed about another goes around it

parts.note: a peasant is a rural labourer
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A fifty-year-old villager can be delightful company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L inside PEASANT; 'A' and 'can be' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasant means agreeable or likeable, close to charming.

clue.text: Query put inside bag that's for packing

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other, so the word for query is placed within

parts.note: to bag something is to get it
to query is to ask

explanation.surface: A question is slipped into a suitcase before a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bag' looks like luggage but is the verb to get. 'that's for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasket is a seal of rubber or similar material fitted between joints, what engineers call packing.

clue.text: American cash held by bank not very long ago

indicators.note: something held by another is enclosed by it

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
a cent is a US coin

explanation.surface: Dollars were lodged with a bank lately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' is the verb to depend, not a lender.
explanation.definitionFit: Recently means lately, a short time back.
